query: For a multi-principal element alloy system known for limited ductility in cast forms, propose a processing route and phase constitution that would simultaneously achieve nanocrystalline grain sizes below 50 nm and a dual-phase solid solution structure, thereby enhancing hardness and yield strength without inducing brittle intermetallic formation. Support this hypothesis with prior evidence regarding grain refinement mechanisms and phase stability limits, define the boundary conditions where this microstructure becomes unstable, and suggest a falsification experiment to distinguish this mechanism from simple solid solution strengthening.

generation.hypothesis: A Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Mo high-entropy alloy system, initially in a cast single-phase FCC solid solution state, can be processed via severe plastic deformation (SPD) followed by controlled low-temperature annealing to achieve a nanocrystalline (<50 nm) dual-phase (FCC + HCP) solid solution structure. This microstructure will simultaneously enhance hardness and yield strength through grain boundary strengthening and phase boundary strengthening, without inducing brittle intermetallic formation, provided Mo content is kept below the solid solution limit (~4 at.%) and carbon is added to stabilize the FCC phase and suppress excessive HCP transformation.
generation.material_initial_state: Cast Co40Cr25(FeNi)35Mo5 high-entropy alloy with single-phase FCC structure and coarse grain size (~47 μm)
generation.intervention: Severe plastic deformation (e.g., high-pressure torsion or equal-channel angular pressing) followed by annealing at 600-700°C for 1-2 hours
generation.conditions: Temperature: 600-700°C; Time: 1-2 hours; Strain rate during SPD: 10^-3 s^-1; Atmosphere: Inert (Ar)
generation.structural_mediator: Nanocrystalline grain boundaries and FCC/HCP phase interfaces acting as barriers to dislocation motion
generation.mechanism: Grain refinement via SPD reduces grain size below 50 nm, while controlled annealing promotes partial FCC-to-HCP transformation to create a dual-phase structure. The dual-phase interface and nanoscale grains provide synergistic strengthening without intermetallic formation due to suppressed diffusion and entropy stabilization.
generation.predicted_outcome: Yield strength increase of >300 MPa, hardness increase of >150 HV, and maintained ductility (>20% elongation) compared to cast state, with no brittle intermetallic phases detected by XRD or TEM.
generation.baseline: Cast Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Mo HEA with single-phase FCC structure and coarse grains, exhibiting yield strength ~400 MPa and elongation ~60%
generation.boundary: Mo content must remain below 4 at.% to avoid Mo carbide formation; annealing temperature must not exceed 700°C to prevent grain growth and excessive HCP transformation; carbon content should be limited to 0.5 at.% to avoid carbide precipitation.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in exact phase fraction and grain size distribution due to local compositional fluctuations and SPD heterogeneity; potential for unexpected intermetallic formation if trace impurities are present.
generation.falsification_experiment: Perform XRD and TEM analysis on the processed alloy to confirm the absence of intermetallic phases and verify the dual-phase FCC/HCP structure with grain size <50 nm. Conduct tensile testing to measure yield strength and elongation. If intermetallic phases are detected or yield strength increase is <200 MPa, the hypothesis is falsified.
